heading: INT. MINIATURE GOLF COURSE - WINDMILL HOLE - DAY

units.text: INT. MINIATURE GOLF COURSE - WINDMILL HOLE - DAY
A garish plastic windmill, a fiberglass dinosaur, a pond of dyed-blue water.
Sprinklers tick.
A line of tourists waits at the tee.
WILLOUGHBY "WILLY" PRATT, 60s, in a golf visor and a pastel polo, grips his putter like a scepter.
His wife, PHILIPPA PRATT, 60s, pats her hair and checks her scorecard.
Their son, CHAD PRATT, 30s, in a collared shirt with the logo of his own startup, scrolls his phone.
Their daughter, PORTIA PRATT, 20s, kicks a tee.
And behind them, the hole's reluctant attendant, MR. DOBBS, 50s, sits in a plastic chair under a beach umbrella, reading a paperback with grim concentration.
The windmill hole. Where families are made or destroyed.
units.name: WILLY

units.text: Please don't be dramatic.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: This is the hole that cost me my first marriage.
units.name: WILLY

units.text: I'm your first marriage.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: That is why it hurt.
units.name: WILLY

units.text: Chad snorts without looking up.
Portia sets her ball on the mat with exaggerated care, takes a stance, and swings.
The ball rolls straight, hits the windmill's spinning blade with a hollow clack, and rebounds.
It rolls back past her feet, past Chad, past Willy's shoes, and into the blue pond with a plop.
That's cheating.
units.name: PORTIA

units.text: It's a windmill.
units.name: MR. DOBBS

units.text: Cheating how?
units.name: WILLY

units.text: The blade moves.
units.name: PORTIA

units.text: That's the idea.
units.name: MR. DOBBS

units.text: Willy hands her another ball.
Philippa lines up her shot with her pinkie extended.

Chad finally pockets his phone, steps up with a stiff practice swing that sends a clod of turf across the course and onto Mr. Dobbs's paperback, and then, with no trace of embarrassment, shrugs and tees up his own ball.
While Willy lectures Portia about wrist angles, Philippa's ball rolls untouched past the windmill, down a slope, and settles at the lip of the hole.
Oh.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: Everyone looks at the ball.
Willy forgets the lecture.
Chad drops his putter.
Portia gasps.
Mr. Dobbs lowers the paperback, revealing a face that has seen this before.
Hole in one?
units.name: WILLY

units.text: Not yet.
units.name: MR. DOBBS

units.text: The windmill blade swings around, taps the ball, and sinks it.
A bell dings.
A tinny fanfare plays from a hidden speaker.
The family goes silent.
Congratulations, ma'am. You win a free game.
units.name: MR. DOBBS

units.text: I do?
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: She does?
units.name: WILLY

units.text: Philippa throws her arms up.
Chad applauds without enthusiasm.
Portia stalks to the pond and begins fishing for her ball with her putter.
Willy sinks onto the dinosaur's tail, defeated.
In forty years, I have never won a free game.
units.name: WILLY

units.text: Darling, you have a free game every time you married me.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: Mr. Dobbs flips a page of his paperback.
Overhead, a plastic seagull swings from a pole, creaking in the wind.
Everyone, finally, laughs, even Willy, even Dobbs, though he hides it behind the book.
Next hole. The one with the volcano.
units.name: WILLY

units.text: Oh, no.
units.name: PHILIPPA

units.text: Dad, the volcano is a lie.
units.name: CHAD

units.text: It is a beautiful lie.
units.name: WILLY

units.text: I got it!
units.name: PORTIA
paren: from the pond, lifting a dripping ball

units.text: She holds it up like a trophy.
Water streams down her arm.
Willy salutes.
The family troops toward the volcano, still bickering, while Mr. Dobbs returns to his paperback and the sprinklers tick on.
